note: Each hand-off between a prompt and a script. tests/test_contracts.py fails when a prompt or script names a file, status, or subcommand that this table does not define, or reads a file that no producer makes.

slice/config.md.form: `- key: value` lines: stack, test command, result format, tests folder, source folders, and the optional `unit tests folder` (separate from `tests folder`), `unit test command`, `source files` (single paths and globs outside the source folders, for example `package.json, migrations/**`), `boundary files` (read-only public interface files for test-writer), and `security scan` (one command that exits non-zero on a finding, for example `bandit -q -r src`; `none` by default)

slice/NNN-<name>/spec.md.form: `Status: draft|ratified` line; requirements as `- Rn (topic): ...`; decisions as `- Dn (topic): ...`

slice/NNN-<name>/slices.md.form: one `## Sn: title` section per slice, with `- Story:`, `- Requirements: R1, R2`, `- Acceptance:`, `- Layers:`, `- Status:`, `- Test rounds:`, `- Review rounds:`

slice/NNN-<name>/domain.md.form: entities, value objects, relationships, invariants, a `### Machine: <Object>` section for each object with a lifecycle (`- States:`, `- Start:`, `- End:`, transitions `- T1: <from> -> <to> on <trigger> [<guard>] / <effect>`, refused lines `- X1: <from> on <trigger> refused: <error>`; the line `- Machines: none` when no object has a lifecycle), the bounded contexts and the boundary, and a `## Requirement map` with one `- Rn: parts` line for each requirement (`GAP` when none; a requirement cites transitions as `Object.T1` or `Object.X1`). `slice.py status` reports a cited transition that no machine defines, a transition that no requirement cites, a machine with no start state, an unreachable state, and a state that States does not list

slice/NNN-<name>/review/Sn.md.form: one `- major: [part] file:line text` or `- minor: [part] file:line text` line for each open code finding, or `none`; part is requirement, architecture, or security. The guard hides it from the test writer

slice/NNN-<name>/review/Sn.tests.md.form: one `- major: [tests] <test name> <what a wrong version would pass, and the fix>` or `- minor: [tests] <test name> <...>` line for each open test finding, or `none`; the wrong version is named as a behaviour, with no test code, no app code, and no file:line. The guard hides it from the implementer. `slice.py commit Sn` refuses on a major line

slice.py next.form: one line: `spec`, `plan`, `domain`, `build Sn`, `stop Sn: reason`, or `done`

tests folder files.form: test files in the tests folder; each test name holds the spec number, the slice ID, and the requirement, `test_NNN_Sn_Rn_<what>` (for example `test_002_S1_R2_counts_words`), the form that `belongs()` of slice.py matches. A name with no number belongs to the slice of the only spec of the project, and to no slice when the project has two specs or more

slice.py scan.form: `scan: none configured`, or `scan: ok`, or `scan: failed (exit N)` (also `scan: failed` for a timeout) followed by at most 6 indented lines of the output of the configured `security scan` command; exit 1 on a failure. `commit Sn` refuses when the scan fails

slice.py test.form: a header `Sn: N tests, P passed, F not passed`, then one `PASS|FAIL|ERROR|SKIP <name>` line for each test of the slice; a FAIL or ERROR line is followed by the `acceptance:` lines of slices.md that cite its requirement (all lines when the name cites none); an ERROR (unittest ERROR, junit error) shows its message indented at once; a FAIL (unittest FAIL, junit failure) shows `message withheld` until the slice has used 2 test rounds, then its message, or at once with `--full` (the guard blocks `--full` for the implementer); then, when a test outside the slice fails (a done slice, or no slice owns it), `regressions: N tests ...` and the same lines for them; `no tests found for Sn` when no test name holds the spec number and the ID
